52:3: Third, he promises liberation from detention by her captors, foretelling the benefit of liberation: loose the bonds, that is, come forth from captivity: I have broken the chains of your necks (Lev 26:13). And he shows the manner of liberation: for thus says the Lord: you were sold gratis, as if to say: those who took you captive furnished no benefits to you; and you shall be redeemed, from captivity to Babylon by Cyrus, above: he shall let go my captives (Isa 45:13); you have sold your people for no price (Ps …
52:4:
For thus says the Lord. Here he assigns two causes of their liberation, namely, the calumny of the people and the blasphemy of God.

And first, he alleges calumny: my people went down into Egypt in the beginning, in their fathers (Gen 46–47); to be a colonist there, and therefore the Egyptians had some right to oppress them from the benefits bestowed on them; and the Assyrian, under which the Chaldeans are also included, has oppressed them without any cause at all, not furnishing them any benefits. …

For thus says the Lord God: My people went down into Egypt at the beginning, to sojourn there; and Assyria oppressed him without any cause. And now what have I here, says the Lord? For my people has been taken away for nothing: its rulers act unjustly, says the Lord, and continually all the day my name is blasphemed. Therefore my people shall know my name in that day: for I myself who spoke, behold, I am here. …
52:5: Second, he pronounces the sentence: for my people is taken away, from their own land; they that rule over them, who have usurped dominion to themselves, namely, the Chaldeans; and, because, my name is continually blasphemed, as though I could not free my people: I will sanctify my great name, which was profaned among the Gentiles (Ezek 36:23).

Hence he adds: And now what have I here, says the Lord? And the sense is: I have nothing left for which I should remain in this region, from which my people has been taken away for nothing, and sold for its sins, and caught like an oryx in a net, either by the forces of the Romans or by the snares of the devil, in which it is held bound to this day. …
52:6: Therefore my people shall know my name in that day, of liberation, for I myself that spoke, promising, I am here, to fulfill my promise: afterwards he was seen upon earth, and conversed with men (Bar 3:38); God, who, at sundry times and in diverse manners, spoke in times past to the fathers by the prophets, last of all, in these days, has spoken to us by his Son (Heb 1:1–2) if this is explained mystically of the coming of Christ.

Therefore he who has the knowledge of the name of God, and is not ignorant that he was created in his image and likeness, will dwell in light. And he will be in the day which Abraham rejoiced to have seen (John 8), of which holy David also speaks: This is the day which the Lord has made, let us exult and rejoice in it (Ps 117 [118]:24). …
52:8: Second, he describes their joy as to the inspection of their watchmen who saw them returning from there, setting out the voice of exultation, the voice, of joy will resound: with one accord lifted up their voice to God (Acts 4:24); and the reason for their joy: for they shall see eye to eye, as if to say, they shall see the captives coming with their own eyes, above: your eyes shall see Jerusalem (Isa 30:20).

And what follows, The voice of your watchmen, or of your guards, signifies the Apostles, of whom God speaks to the Church in another place too (below, Isa 62:6): Upon your walls I have set guards, who shall never be silent, remembering the Lord, who will lift up their voice, discoursing of lofty things. Hence it is said to them (above, Isa 40:9): Go up upon a high mountain, you who bring good news to Zion. Lift up your voice with strength, you who bring good news to Jerusalem. …
52:9: Third, as to the arrival of the captives: rejoice, above: the land that was desolate shall be glad, and the wilderness shall rejoice (Isa 35:1).

Rejoice and praise together, deserts of Jerusalem, for the Lord has comforted his people: he has redeemed Jerusalem. The Lord has prepared his holy arm in the eyes of all the nations: and all the ends of the earth shall see the salvation of our God. LXX: Let the deserts of Jerusalem break forth into gladness together, for the Lord has had mercy on her, and has rescued Jerusalem. The Lord will reveal his holy arm in the sight of all the nations. And all the ends of the earth shall see the salvation of our God. …
53:10:
If he shall lay down. Here he sets out that, through him, the justification of men was completed.

And first, he sets out the reward for the sorrow of his death: if he shall lay down his life, of his own will: I lay down my life (John 10:17), he shall see a long-lived seed, until the end of the world, sons for him reborn out of the power of his death: unless the grain of wheat falling into the ground die, itself remains alone. …

And the Lord willed to cleanse him from the stroke which he had received when pierced by the soldier's lance. Or to bruise him in infirmity and wound; of which he himself also said: For they persecuted him whom you struck (Ps 68 [69]:27). And through Zechariah God says: I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep shall be scattered (Zech 13:7). Therefore his suffering was not of necessity, but of the will of the Father and of his own, he who said to him: O God, to do your will, I have willed it (Ps 39 [40]:9). …
53:4: Second, as to his exposed infirmity, he sets out the sign of his infirmity: truly, as true man, he has borne, suffered, our infirmities, infirmities, such as hunger and thirst, and carried our sorrows, of sense, in suffering and sadness; or, our infirmities, our sins, he has taken from us; or in our place, he has suffered punishments: he bore our sins in his body upon the tree (1 Pet 2:24). …

He truly bore our sicknesses and sins, and suffers pain for us, not in seeming, that is, τὸ δοκεῖν, as an old and a new heresy suppose; but he was truly crucified. He truly suffered pain, saying in the Gospel: My soul is sorrowful even unto death (Matt 26:38). And: Now my soul is troubled (John 12:27). And we thought him unclean, or in pain, as the Seventy translated; for which Aquila and Symmachus put leprous, Theodotion scourged. …
53:5:
But he was wounded. Here he sets out the fruit of his humiliation or of his passion.

And first, he assigns the moving reason: but he was, not as we thought, but wounded, by thorns, nails, and lance, for our iniquities, taking them away, he was bruised, by scourges and blows. Or he was wounded, as to where the previous verse says: he was struck; he was bruised, as to where it says: afflicted: the breath of our mouth, Christ the Lord, is taken in our sins (Lam 4:20).

 …

But he was wounded for our iniquities, he was bruised for our crimes. The discipline of our peace was upon him, and by his bruise we have been healed. All we like sheep have gone astray, each one in his own way has turned aside: and the Lord has laid on him the iniquity of us all. He was offered because he himself willed it, and he did not open his mouth. LXX: But he was wounded for our sins, and was weakened for our iniquities. The discipline of our peace was upon him: by his bruise we have been healed. …
53:6: Third, he shows the imminent necessity on our part, for all are sick, and thus all need a physician, and no one else can offer a sufficient remedy: for there is no distinction of Jew and Greek, for all have sinned and do need (Rom 3:22–23) penance; all we like sheep have gone astray: for you were as sheep without a shepherd (1 Pet 2:25).

All, he says, like sheep have gone astray, and we have needed the mercy of God, saying in the psalm: I have gone astray like a lost sheep (Ps 118 [119]:176); the sheep which in the parable of the Gospel was carried back on the shoulders of the good and careful Shepherd (Matt 18). And who these sheep are, the following verse shows: Man has gone astray in his own way; or each one has turned aside in his own way, to follow his own error, and, forsaking the right way, to hold differing opinions about the Crucified. …
54:10: Second, from the operation of stable creatures: for the mountains shall be moved, as if to say: it is easier for mountains and hills to be changed than for my words to be made void. Or, by mountains and hills, the powerful of the earth are signified: we will not fear, when the earth shall be troubled (Ps 45:3[46:2]).
54:11:
986. O poor little one. Here he promises prosperity as a remedy against adversity.

And first, he recalls their former adversity: O poor little one, Jerusalem despoiled of goods; tossed with tempest, of adversity, above: to a nation rent and torn in pieces (Isa 18:2). I will send you.

Second, he promises future prosperity.

 …

Poor little one, torn by the tempest, without consolation. Behold, I will lay your stones in order: and I will found you on sapphires: and I will make your battlements of jasper, and your gates of carved stones, and all your borders of desirable stones: All your sons taught by the Lord, and a multitude of peace for your sons, and in righteousness you shall be founded. LXX: Lowly and unstable, without consolation. …
54:14:
And as to justice of works, and you shall be founded in justice, above: Zion shall be redeemed in judgment, and they shall bring her back in justice (Isa 1:27).

987. Second, as to freedom from evils, first, promising deliverance from dangers: depart, that is, you shall depart, for you shall not suffer calumny: he shall humble the calumniators (Ps 71[72]:4).

Withdraw far from calumny, for you shall not fear; and from terror, for it shall not come near you. LXX: Withdraw from the unjust man, and you shall not fear, and trembling shall not come near you. A most beautiful order. He had consoled the poor and lowly one, promising her spiritual graces. Now he teaches what she ought to do if she does not wish to dread the assaults of her adversaries. And the sense is: You do not wish to fear your enemies? …
54:15: Second, the adherence of strangers: behold, an inhabitant shall come, for many from the gentiles adhered to them when they came out of captivity, below: let not the son of the stranger, that adheres to the Lord, speak, saying: the Lord will divide and separate me from his people (Isa 56:3).

Behold, the sojourner shall come who was not with me; he who was once a stranger to you shall be joined to you. LXX: Behold, proselytes shall come to you through me, and they shall be your settlers, and shall flee to you for refuge. These things too the Jews think are said to Jerusalem: that many of the nations will be proselytes and will take up the law of Moses and its ceremonies. …
54:16:
Third, he promises the destruction of their enemies: behold, I.

And first, he shows the power of the one who promises, setting out a similitude: I have created the smith, the persecutor, who blows in the fire of tribulation, instruments, adversaries, according to his own will: his breath kindles coals (Job 41:12[21]); and he explains this: I have created the killer to destroy: the Lord kills and makes alive (1 Sam 2:6).

Behold, I have created the smith who blows the coals in the fire, and brings forth a vessel for his work: and I have created the slayer to destroy. Every vessel that is fashioned against you shall not prosper: and every tongue that resists you in judgment you shall judge. This is the inheritance of the servants of the Lord: and their righteousness is with me, says the Lord. LXX: Behold, I have created you, not as a coppersmith blowing the coals in the fire and bringing forth a vessel for work. …
54:17: Second, he sets out the promise: no vessel that is formed against you shall prosper, that is, he will scatter everything formed, as to those attacking with deeds, and every tongue, as to those attacking with words, above: they shall be as nothing (Isa 41:11).

And all who have been fashioned against you by the blowing smith shall not prosper, but shall feel both present punishments and those to come. And what before seemed hidden is said more plainly in what follows: And every tongue that resists you in judgment you shall judge, destroying the wisdom of the wise and rejecting the prudence of the prudent. …
54:2: 978. Second, he exhorts them to enlarge their place under the metaphor of a tent: enlarge the place, as to the ground over which the tent is extended; and stretch out the skins, with which it is covered; lengthen your cords, with which the stakes are tied; and strengthen your nails, with which the boards are joined, or the stakes themselves. And we read that these things were in the tabernacle of the covenant (Exod 26 and 36). …

Enlarge the place of your tent, and stretch out the skins of your tabernacles: do not spare: make your cords long, and make your stakes firm. For you shall penetrate to the right and to the left, and your seed shall inherit the nations, and shall inhabit the deserted cities. LXX: Enlarge the place of your tabernacle, and fix the skins of your curtains, do not spare. …
54:3: 979. Third, he foretells their fulfillment of the exhortation: for you shall pass on to the right hand, and to the left, as if to say: you shall increase in every direction. This was fulfilled in the time of the Maccabees, when certain cities of the region of Samaria and other regions were added to the kingdom of the Jews: may your seed possess the gates of their enemies (Gen 24:60).
54:4:
980. Fear not. Here he promises the restoration of their former honor as a remedy against the confusion which they had sustained earlier;

second, he sets out the firmness of the promise: this thing is to me as in the days of Noah (Isa 54:9).

Concerning the first, he does two things.

 …

Do not fear, for you shall not be confounded, nor shall you blush: for you shall not be ashamed, because you shall forget the confusion of your youth, and shall no more remember the reproach of your widowhood. For He who made you shall rule over you, the Lord of hosts is His name: and your redeemer, the Holy One of Israel, shall be called the God of all the earth. …
54:5:
981. Second, he promises the restoration of their former honor.

And first, he sets out restoration as to dominion: for he that made you shall rule over you, above: O Lord, other lords besides you have had dominion over us (Isa 26:13).
54:6: And as to marriage: for the Lord has called you as a woman forsaken: if a man put away his wife, and she go from him, and marry another man, shall he return to her any more? (Jer 3:1).

For the Lord has called you as a woman forsaken and mourning in spirit: and as a wife cast off from her youth, says your God. For a moment, for a little while, I forsook you: and with great mercies I will gather you. In a moment of indignation I hid my face from you for a little while: and with everlasting mercy I have had pity on you, says your redeemer, the Lord. LXX: Not as a woman forsaken and faint-hearted has the Lord called you, nor as a woman who is hated from her youth, says your God. …
54:7:
Second, he promises increase of honor as to the great number of honors: said your God, for a small moment, you have suffered in respect of the things which, taking pity, I will grant you: for that which is at present, is momentary (2 Cor 4:17).

985. Note also on the words, with great mercies (Isa 54:7), that the mercies to come are great:

first, because they are interior: for I reckon that the sufferings of this time are not worthy to be compared with the glory to come that shall be revealed in us (Rom 8:18);

 …
54:8: And as to their duration, in a moment, as if to say: for a short time you have felt my wrath in respect to the time in which I will have mercy on you, above: hide yourself a little for a moment (Isa 26:20). All these things which have been said are mystically explained of the calling of the gentiles, for heathendom was at first barren, but afterwards gathered many children, according to the Gloss.
54:9:
982. This thing is to me as in the days of Noah. Here he shows the firmness of the promise.

And first, from a similitude with an earlier promise: to whom I swore, firmly established, if only you remain in my commandments: I will establish my covenant with you, and with your seed after you (Gen 9:9); the covenants of the world were made with him, that all flesh should no more be destroyed with the flood (Sir 44:19[18]).

As in the days of Noah, so is this to me, to whom I swore that I would no more bring the waters of Noah upon the earth: so I have sworn not to be angry with you and not to rebuke you. For the mountains shall be moved, and the hills shall tremble: but my mercy shall not depart from you, and the covenant of my peace shall not be moved, says the Lord who has compassion on you. …
55:10: And as the rain and the snow. Here he shows the firmness of the promise: And first, he sets out the efficacy of the divine word: it shall not return to me void, that is, without fruit: an obscure speech shall not go for naught (Wis 1:11); he will come to us as the early and the latter rain to the earth (Hos 6:3).

Or certainly this is to be said, that the word of the Gospel's teaching is called rain, and the showers which the spiritual clouds pour upon the good earth, the clouds to which the truth of God reaches. This rain and these showers Moses promises in the Song of Deuteronomy (Deut 32:1, 2): Let the earth hear the words of my mouth: let my speech be awaited as the rain, and let my words come down as the dew; so that those who have sown in tears may reap in joy (Ps 125 [126]). …
55:12: Second, he sets out restraint as to their joyful release from Babylon, for you shall go out with joy: he brought forth his people with joy, and his chosen with gladness (Ps 104[105]:43); as to the congratulations of others: the mountains and the hills, the powerful and the common people, praising God in you; or this is hyperbole: your land congratulating your return.

For you shall go out in gladness, and be led forth in peace. The mountains and the hills shall sing praise before you, and all the trees of the country shall clap their hands. Instead of the saliunca the fir shall come up, and instead of the nettle the myrtle shall grow. And the Lord shall be named for an everlasting sign, which shall not be taken away. LXX: In gladness you shall go out, and in joy you shall be led forth. …
55:13:
As to the multiplied restoration of goods: instead of the shrub, shall come up the fir tree, that is, your former goods are few in comparison to what you will have: the glory of this last house shall be more than of the first (Hag 2:10[9]), above: I will plant in the wilderness the cedar (Isa 41:19). The shrub (saliuncula) from saliendo ("jumping"), which is called "hare thistle."

 …

And not only shall the mountains and hills leap and sing, and all the trees of the field which the Lord has blessed clap with their branches and applaud with their hands, but the στοιβή too and the κονύζη, or the saliunca and the nettle, shall be turned into the fir and the myrtle and the cypress. Στοιβή, according to Symmachus and the Seventy, is written in the Hebrew NESUS (נעצוץ), which Aquila and Theodotion interpreted as κονύζην. Now κονύζη is a most worthless and bitter herb, of a very foul smell. …
55:2:
And he recalls their former poverty, why do you spend money for that which is not bread? As if to say: why thus far have you been spending money and from it have not been able to eat bread? You have sowed much, and brought in little (Hag 1:6). These things, however, are explained mystically of the water of divine wisdom, which is given freely to the thirsty, according to the Gloss.

 …

Hear, you who hear me, and eat what is good, and your soul shall delight in fatness. Incline your ear, and come to me: hear, and your soul shall live. And I will strike with you an everlasting covenant: the faithful mercies of David. LXX: Hear me, and eat good things, and your soul shall delight in good things. Attend with your ears, and follow my ways: and hear me, and your soul shall live in good things. And I will establish for you an eternal testament, the faithful holy things of David. …
55:3:
Second, he promises escape from death: incline your ear: my soul shall live (Ps 118[119]:175); and also: your justifications I will never forget: for by them you have given me life (Ps 118[119]:93).

Third, he promises power. And first, he sets out a similitude: and I will make an everlasting covenant, the faithful mercies of David, that is, as I made true promises to David that his seed would remain forever, so I will also do with you.

Finally he adds: Hear me, and your soul shall live (Isa 55:3). The promise of all good things is life everlasting. If you are willing to hear, and your soul lives forever, I will strike with you an everlasting covenant, the faithful mercies of David. Of these the same Psalmist sang: The mercies of the Lord I will sing forever. From generation to generation I will proclaim your truth (Ps 88 [89]:1, 2). …
55:4: Second, he explains this similitude, showing what he did for David: behold I have given him for a witness to the people: a people which I knew not, has served me: at the hearing of the ear they have obeyed me (Ps 17:45[18:44]).

Behold, I have given him as a witness to the peoples, a leader and teacher to the nations. Behold, you shall call a nation which you did not know: and nations which have not known you shall run to you, because of the Lord your God and the Holy One of Israel, because He has glorified you. …
55:5: And what may be done for them: behold you shall call nations, to fulfill your command, not by your own power, but because of the Lord, above: and they shall adore for the sake of the Lord your God, who has chosen you (Isa 49:7).
55:7:
Second, he teaches the manner of seeking: let the wicked, sinning against God, forsake his way, and the unjust man, sinning against his neighbor, above: take away the evil of your devices from my eyes (Isa 1:16).

Third, he sets out the fruit of returning, namely, mercy: and let him return to the Lord, and he will have mercy on him; for he is bountiful, that is, of manifold mercy, to forgive: turn to the Lord your God: for he is gracious and merciful (Joel 2:13–14).

Nor is it enough to seek the Lord, and to find Him while it is the time of repentance, and to call upon Him while He is near, unless the ungodly man forsakes his former ways and the old thoughts by which he had turned aside from the Lord. …
56:1: Thus says the Lord: Keep judgment, and do righteousness: for my salvation is near to come, and my righteousness to be revealed. For righteousness the Seventy translated mercy; the rest alike. The prophecy about the nations being ended, which at the coming of the word of God are to be changed from saliunca and nettle into cypress and myrtle, Isaiah speaks to the hearers of that time, that they should do all things that are right and prepare themselves for the coming of the Savior, because He Himself is the …
56:11:
In plundering their goods: and most impudent dogs, plundering their subjects of their goods as if without any bridle of shame, and they are never satisfied: they shall suffer hunger like dogs (Ps 58:7[59:6]); and as to lack in perfection of knowledge: the shepherds themselves knew no understanding, of the law and the prophets: he that understands shall possess governments (Prov 1:5); they have not known nor understood: they walk on in darkness (Ps 81[82]:5).

 …

And what follows: Each to his own avarice, from the highest to the last: come, let us take wine, and be filled with drunkenness, and it shall be as today, so also tomorrow, and much more, is not found in the Seventy Translators, but has been added from the Hebrew and is marked beforehand with shining stars. In short, none of the Church's interpreters has expounded these little verses, but they leap over them and pass them by, as if a pit lay open in the middle of the road. …
56:12: Third, as to pleasure, which pertains to concupiscence of the flesh: come, let us take wine, and it shall be, that is, if today we rejoice in such things, to morrow, much more, above: behold joy and gladness, killing calves, and slaying rams, eating flesh, and drinking wine (Isa 22:13).
56:2:
Blessed is the man. Here he sets out the fruit of this counsel in those who receive it.

And first, he sets out its utility, setting out the fruit of fulfilling it: blessed is the man that doth this, fulfilling it by his works, and the son of man that shall lay hold on this, undertaking it strenuously: blessed is the man that fears the Lord (Ps 111[112]:1); and the manner of fulfilling it, as to ceremonial precepts: that keeps the sabbath. …

Blessed is the man who does this, and the son of man who lays hold of it: keeping the sabbath, so as not to profane it: keeping his hands, so as not to do any evil. LXX: Blessed is the man who shall do these things, and the man who holds them fast, and keeps the sabbaths, so as not to profane them, and guards his hands, so as not to do iniquity. …
56:3:
Second, he sets out the universality of this utility: and let not the son of the stranger.

And first, he excludes the desperation of some who seemed unworthy, either because of defect of race, because they were not of the race of Israel: that adheres to the Lord, keeping his precepts; saying: the Lord will divide and separate me from his people, not making me a sharer in the salvation promised to them: for there is no distinction of the Jew and the Greek: for the same is Lord over all (Rom 10:12). …

Those who please me are those who choose to be eunuchs voluntarily.… Who can receive this teaching, let him receive it. It is a matter of great faith and great virtue to be the purest kind of temple of God, in that one dedicates oneself completely to the Lord as a burnt offering and to be holy in body as well as spirit. Those are eunuchs who, thinking themselves to be "dry trees" because of their infertility, hear through Isaiah that instead of sons and daughters they will have a place prepared in heaven. …
56:4: Second, he sets out the promise: for thus says the Lord. And first, in those things pertaining especially to eunuchs: they that shall keep my sabbaths, as to religious worship, and shall choose the things that please me, as to obedience of the law, and shall hold fast my covenant, as to observance of the promise to abstain from evils.

For thus says the Lord to the eunuchs: If they keep my sabbaths, and choose the things I have willed, and hold fast my covenant, I will give them in my house and within my walls a place, and a name better than sons and daughters: an everlasting name I will give them, which shall not perish. …
56:5:
Within my walls, a place, that is, a dwelling within the walls of my city; and a name better, because they will be called my servants and holy ones, and sons, that is, as if they had begotten many sons: the eunuch, that has not wrought iniquity (Wis 3:14).

Note on the words, I will give to them . . . a name better, that the saints have a name

first, from predestination, above: the Lord has called me from the womb, from the bowels of my mother he has been mindful of my name (Isa 49:1);

 …
56:6:
And as to foreigners: and the children of the stranger, that is, I will give them the privileges in which the Jews glory, to worship him, as to special worship, and to love his name, like children, to be his servants, and to glory in his dominion, above: they shall worship the Lord (Isa 19:21). And these things were indeed fulfilled in the return of the people from captivity, but more fully in the conversion of the gentiles to the faith of Christ, as to the Gloss explains.

 …

Is it not written, "He says, 'My house shall be called a house of prayer for all the nations' "? We read this in Isaiah: "But you have made it a den of thieves." …Where we read, "You have made it a den of thieves," John's Gospel had instead, "You have made it a house of business." Wherever there are thieves, there is a house of trafficking. Would that it were applied only to the Jews and not the Christians! We would, indeed, weep for them but rejoice for ourselves. …
56:8: Second, as to the gathering of the people: the Lord God, who gathers, to him, Israel, the peoples who adhere to him: the Lord builds up Jerusalem: he will gather together the dispersed of Israel (Ps 146[147]:2).

These things the Lord promised would be, He who gathers the scattered of Israel; to whom the Apostle Peter also writes an Epistle; of whom the Evangelist says: This he did not say of himself, but, being high priest that year, he prophesied that Jesus was to die for the nation, and not for the nation only, but that He might gather into one the sons of God who were scattered (John 11:51, 52); and that might be fulfilled which was said: The congregation of the peoples shall surround you: for its sake return on high …
56:9:
All you beasts of the field. Here he threatens lack of salvation to those who hold his counsel in contempt.

And first, he designates the punishment of killing: all you beasts of the field come to devour, their corpses: say to every fowl (Ezek 39:17).

And when the remnant of Israel had been gathered through the Apostles, and those who before had been scattered had been brought into one flock, all the beasts are summoned to come and devour Israel, namely those who would not believe, of whom the Apostle says: For the end shall come upon them (Phil 3). And the Lord in the Gospel: But when you see Jerusalem surrounded by an army, then know that its consummation has come (Luke 21:20). …
57:10:
You have been wearied in the multitude of your ways. Here he shows their obstinacy in sin.

First, because they were not recalled by the labor of sin: you have been wearied in the multitude of your ways, that is, in the manifold cult of idols: we wearied ourselves in the way of iniquity and destruction (Wis 5:7).

 …

In the multitude of your way you have labored, and you did not say: I will rest. You have found the life of your hand; therefore you have not asked me. LXX: In your many journeys you have labored, and you did not say: I will leave off. Strengthened, you have done these things; therefore you have not asked me. He who walks in the one royal way does not labor, the way about which God commanded through Moses: You shall walk in the royal way, and you shall not turn aside to the right or to the left (Deut 5:32). …

And first, as to merchandise, he sets out beasts of burden: the flood, that is, an abundance like a flood of water, of camels, on which merchandise was carried; which signifies, mystically, the rich, turned to faith, who carry the burden of riches and the hump of sin, above: they carry their riches upon the shoulders of beasts (Isa 30:6); dromedaries, an animal smaller than a camel, but swifter; which signifies nations converted swiftly to the faith; Madian and Epha, regions …

And again I say to you: It is easier for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter the kingdom of heaven. By this saying it is shown that it is not difficult but impossible. For if, as a camel cannot enter through the eye of a needle, so a rich man cannot enter the kingdom of heaven, none of the rich will be saved. …
60:7: Second, as to clean animals, inasmuch as they were granted to be used for food: all the flocks of Cedar, the son of Ismael, from whom a land, which abounds in sheep, has its name; the rams of Nabaioth, another son of Ismael; shall minister to you, be granted for your use, sold to the people who are in you; and inasmuch as they were granted for the use of sacrifices: they shall be offered upon my acceptable altar, that is, in which I am pleased. …
60:8: Who are these who fly like clouds, and like doves to their windows? For the islands wait for me, and the ships of the sea in the beginning, that I may bring your sons from afar, their silver and their gold with them, to the name of the Lord your God, and to the Holy One of Israel, because he has glorified you. LXX: Who are these who fly like clouds, and like doves with their young to me? …
60:9: And he sets out the help in coming, which they had from the gentiles: the islands, the various nations by the sea, and even far off, wait for me, as though subject to the choice of my will; the ships of the sea from the beginning of the place in which they were held captive, for perhaps some returned through the sea, or the Lord was able to lead them back thus. …
61:1:
1073. The spirit of the Lord is upon me. Here he promises joy to the people. And this is divided into two parts:

in the first, he promises joy;

in the second, the people receive the promise and give thanks, where it says, I will greatly rejoice in the Lord (Isa 61:10).

Concerning the first, he does two things:

first, he accepts the office of announcing joy;

second, he foretells the reason or the matter of this joy: and they shall be called (Isa 61:3).

1074. Concerning the first, he does two things.

 …

The Spirit of the Lord God is upon me, because the Lord has anointed me; he has sent me to bring good news to the meek, to heal the broken in heart, and to preach indulgence to the captives, and opening to those who are shut in; and to proclaim a year of favor to the Lord, and a day of vengeance to our God; to comfort all who mourn; to appoint for those who mourn in Zion, and to give them a crown instead of ashes, the oil of joy instead of mourning, a mantle of praise instead of a spirit of sorrow. …
61:11: Third, under the likeness of buds, as to their fruits: for as the earth brings forth her bud, above: it shall bud forth and blossom, and shall rejoice with joy and praise (Isa 35:2).

And she sets forth examples of another comparison, of which the first refers to the bridegroom, the next to the bride. As the earth brings forth its shoot and is watered by the rains of heaven, and as a garden makes its seed spring up, which longs for the waters of springs and rivers, so, he says, the Lord will make righteousness and gladness spring up before all the nations: by no means before Israel, so as to strike down the haughtiness of the Jews, but before all the nations, which are gathered in the Church.
61:2:
And the time of liberation: to proclaim the acceptable year of the Lord, as to the liberation of the Jews, and the day of vengeance, as to the Chaldeans; or the time of grace, in which he takes vengeance upon the devil, curbing his power: now is the judgment of the world: now shall the prince of this world be cast out (John 12:31); you shall bless the crown of the year of your goodness (Ps 64:12[65:11]); for the time is come (Ps 101:14[102:13]).

1076. …

And he comforted all who mourn, saying: Blessed are those who mourn, for they shall be comforted (Matt 5:5), so that he might appoint for those who mourn in Zion, and give them glory and a crown instead of ashes. Among these was the apostle Paul too, who mourned for Zion and said: For I have sorrow and continual grief (Rom 9:2); and again: I could wish that I myself were anathema from Christ for my brethren and kinsmen according to the flesh, who are Israelites (ibid., 3). …
61:3:
To appoint to the mourners of Zion, in particular: with a great spirit he saw the things that are to come to pass at last, and comforted the mourners in Zion (Sir 48:27); and the sign of joy, when the signs of sadness are turned to signs of gladness, and this is and to give them a crown for ashes, above: in that day the Lord shall be a crown of glory (Isa 28:5).

1077. And they shall be called. Here he foretells the matter of their joy. …

And in her they will be called the mighty ones of righteousness, the planting of the Lord for glorifying. And they will build the places deserted from of old, and raise up the ancient ruins, and restore the cities deserted and scattered from generation to generation. And strangers will stand and feed your flocks, and the sons of foreigners will be your farmers and vinedressers. LXX: And they will be called generations of righteousness, the planting of the Lord for glory. …
61:4: And the restoration of buildings, and they shall build, these same men, or the apostles, above: and the places that have been desolate for ages shall be built in you (Isa 58:12).
61:5: 1078. Second, as to the keeping of their possessions: and strangers shall stand. This could be fulfilled literally, as some foreigners were employed in these menial services, like the Gabaonites: so let them live, as to serve the whole multitude (Josh 9:21); or mystically: the gentile preachers, flocks: the simple believers of the Church, and these keep and cultivate the Church herself by their merits and teaching.

They will have not only the skill of building and restoring cities, but they will also be the best of shepherds, so that, the old shepherds being driven away, to whom God had said through Ezekiel, O shepherds of Israel, do shepherds feed themselves, and not rather the sheep (Ezek 34:2)?, they may hear with the apostle Peter: Feed my sheep (John 21:17). …
61:6:
1081. But you shall be called the priests. Here he foretells the matter of joy as to the glory of men. And concerning this, he does three things.

First, he shows the perfection of their glory, because they are glorious in spiritual things: priests, as living a holy life worthy of priesthood, as 2 Kings 8:18 says of the sons of David: how they are numbered among the children of God, and their lot is among the saints (Wis 5:5); they are glorious, too, in temporal things: you shall eat the strength of the Gentiles, …

But you will be called the priests of the Lord; it will be said to you, ministers of our God. You will eat the strength of the nations, and you will pride yourselves in their glory. Instead of your double confusion and shame they will praise their portion; therefore in their land they will possess double things; everlasting gladness will be theirs; for I am the Lord who loves judgment, and hates robbery in burnt offering. LXX: But you will be called the priests of the Lord, ministers of our God. …
61:7:
1082. And he assigns the reason for the perfection: for your double confusion, as if to say: you had confusion from lack of spiritual and temporal things; they shall praise, that is, your neighbors, seeing, their part, the recompense of double goods, made to them by God: I will render you double as I declare today (Zech 9:12). Mystically: the Church receives rewards in the goods of soul and body for the double confusion from the faithlessness of the gentiles and the Jews.

1083. …

And what follows, Instead of double confusion and instead of shame they will praise their portion, which is not found in the Seventy, I think should be explained thus: Because you had a double confusion, both over the people of the Jews, which had departed from God, and over the nations, which served idols, you will see them, converted to the fear of God, praising their portion: without doubt the Lord, of whom the holy man also spoke: My portion is the Lord (Ps 72 [73]:26). …
61:8: And he assigns the reason: for I am the Lord. And this is the sense: because the Lord loves justice, he will grant to you that you will be just, that thus you may be pleasing to him, and he will make a covenant with you of everlasting joy; I hate robbery in a holocaust: he that offers sacrifice of the goods of the poor, is as one that sacrifices the son in the presence of his father (Sir 34:24); a perpetual covenant: and I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel, and with the house of Judah (Jer 31:31).

And I will give their work in truth, and I will strike an everlasting covenant with them. And their seed will be known among the nations, and their offspring in the midst of the peoples. All who see them will recognize them, that these are the seed which the Lord has blessed. LXX: And I will give their labor to the righteous, and I will set an eternal testament with them. And their seed will be known among the nations, and their descendants in the midst of the peoples. …

And then the apostolic seed will be known among the nations, and all future generations will receive the sowing of God's doctrine; by no means saying that in which the people of the circumcision formerly erred, saying: For what else does God seek but seed? Everyone who sees them will recognize at first sight that they are the seed which the Lord has blessed. For who would not recognize the people of God from their manner of life, their gentleness, continence, hospitality and all their virtues? …

second, the promise of the Lord: the Lord has sworn (Isa 62:8).

first, he himself asks;

 …

And he will call, he says, them, the Lord and Savior himself. Or, according to the Hebrew, they will call them, the Apostles and apostolic men, a holy people, and redeemed by the Lord, who have been redeemed by the blood of Christ. …

First, as to the glory of the city, promising this glory in three things.

In the dignity of the king: and the Gentiles shall see, admiring and revering, your just one, Christ or Cyrus: all the ends of the earth have seen the salvation of our God (Ps 97[98]:3).

62:3: In the defense of divine protection: and you shall be a crown of glory, because your God will glory in you, as a king glories in the crown of his kingdom; in the hand of the Lord, that is, in his protection: they shall receive a kingdom of glory, and a crown of beauty at the hand of the Lord (Wis 5:17). You will no longer be called Forsaken, and your land will no more be called Desolate; but you will be called My-will-is-in-her, and your land Inhabited, for the Lord has been well pleased in you, and your land will be inhabited. LXX: And you will no longer be called Forsaken, and your land will not be called Deserted any more. For you will be called My will, and your land Inhabited. Instead of Zion and Jerusalem you will be called the Church and the Lord's; instead of Jews they will be called Christians. …
62:5: 1089. Second, as to the joy of the inhabitants of the city; both as to boys: for the young man shall dwell with the virgin; and as to grown men: and your sons shall dwell in you; and as to married men: and the bridegroom shall rejoice over the bride: there shall be heard again in this place (Jer 33:10). Mystically: the young man shall dwell with the virgin, chastely, as Mary dwelled with Joseph; the bridegroom, Christ; the bride, the Church.

For the young man will dwell with the virgin, and your sons will dwell in you. And the bridegroom will rejoice over the bride; your God will rejoice over you. LXX: And as a young man dwelling with a virgin, so will your sons dwell. And it will be that as a bridegroom is glad over a bride, so the Lord will be glad over you. The Apostle too says: Husbands, love your wives, as Christ also loved the Church (Eph 5:25). …

Upon your walls, Jerusalem, I have set watchmen; all the day and all the night they will never be silent. You who remember the Lord, do not be silent, and give him no silence, until he establishes, and until he makes Jerusalem a praise in the earth. LXX: And upon your walls, Jerusalem, I have set watchmen, all the day and all the night, who will never be silent, remembering the Lord: for there is none like you if he corrects, and he will make Jerusalem a joy upon the earth. …

1092. The Lord has sworn by his right hand. Here the Lord promises to fulfill the petition.

And first, as to driving back their enemies: if, supply: you do not trust in me, I will give your corn to be meat for your enemies: he that tills his ground (Prov 28:19), and eats not the fruit from it.

The Lord has sworn by his right hand and by the arm of his strength: If I give your wheat any more as food to your enemies, and if the sons of strangers drink your wine, for which you have labored! For those who gather it will eat it and praise the Lord, and those who bring it in will drink it in my holy courts. …
63:1: Furthermore, because Idumea means both earthly and, on account of the color red, can also be understood as bloody, for this reason the Savior, carrying back to the Father the victory over the world, when the angels were crying out: Open your gates, O princes, and the king of glory shall enter in. And in Isaiah, astonished, they were asking: Who is this who comes up from Edom, with garments tawny from Bozrah, so beautiful in a white robe? …
63:10:
1107. Second, he touches on the benefits as to the remission of faults.

And first, he sets out their fault: but they; his spirit, namely God's, or the spirit of his Holy One, Moses, through their various quarrels: and Moses was afflicted for their sakes, because they exasperated his spirit (Ps 105[106]:32–33).

Second, he sets out their punishment: and he, namely, God, was turned to be their enemy: the Lord is become as an enemy (Lam 2:5); you are changed to be cruel toward me (Job 30:21).

But if the prudent reader should answer in silent thought, Why have many not been saved, if he himself saved them, and loved and spared his sons, and redeemed them with his blood, and took them up and exalted them once assumed?, a clear reason is given: But they did not believe, and they embittered his Holy Spirit, or the Spirit of his Holy One, which in Hebrew is CADESO (קדש). …
63:11:
Third, he sets out the remission of the fault: and he remembered, at last, Moses, who prayed for them: either forgive them, or strike me out of the book that you have written (Exod 32:31–32); he has remembered his covenant for ever: the word which he commanded to a thousand generations (Ps 104[105]:8).

1109. Where is he that brought them up? Here he laments the same benefits taken away from them.

 …

And he remembered the days of the age, of Moses, of his people. Where is he who brought them up out of the sea with the shepherds of his flock? Where is he who put in its midst the Spirit of his Holy One? Who led Moses by the right hand with the arm of his majesty; who divided the waters before them, to make for himself an everlasting name; who led them through the depths like a horse in the desert that does not stumble. …
63:12: By the right hand, prosperously; where is the spirit that divided the waters before them? Who divided the Red Sea into parts (Ps 135[136]:13).
63:13: And where is he that led them out as a horse that stumbles not, namely, without hindrance.

For he led his people through the boundless depths of the waters like a horse through the wilderness, and like cattle over the plain, and the Spirit of the Lord was its leader, that is, of the Lord's flock (Exod 14). By Spirit here we ought to understand the angel who was the leader of the people of Israel, according to what is written: Who makes his angels spirits, and his ministers a burning fire (Ps 103 [104]:4). …
63:14: As a beast that goes down, with an unhindered course; the spirit of the Lord was their, the people's, leader: and in the Red Sea a way without hindrance (Wis 19:7); they shall walk confidently (Prov 3:23); where are his miracles? (Judg 6:13).
63:15:
1110. Second, he inclines the judge to affection.

And first, he seeks a hearing: look down from heaven: you will hear from your holy heaven (1 Kgs 8:32).

Second, he provokes him to mercy: where is your zeal with which you loved us. Lord, where are your ancient mercies? (Ps 88:50[89:49]); if he withhold the waters, all things shall be dried up (Job 12:15).

Look down from heaven, and see from your holy dwelling and that of your glory. Where is your zeal and your strength? The multitude of your bowels and of your mercies toward me have held themselves back. For you are our father; and Abraham has not known us, and Israel has been ignorant of us. You, O Lord, are our father, our redeemer from of old is your name. LXX: Turn from heaven, and see from your holy house and that of your glory: where is your zeal and your strength? …
63:16: Third, he sets out a cause for having mercy: for you are our father, and Abraham has not known us, when he was still alive, because we did not then exist; or, even now, he is unwilling to pray for us, because we do not call upon him; or, according to Augustine, because the dead, even the saints, do not know what is to be done for the living: but this is to be understood as to the power of human knowledge, not as to the illumination of divine light: he is your father, that has possessed you, and made you, and …

For you, he says, are our father, you who are the creator of all. Abraham does not know us, and Israel is ignorant of us, because we have offended you, nor do they recognize as sons those whom they perceive not to be loved by their God. A sudden question arises: why did he set down Abraham and Israel, that is, Jacob, and leave the name of Isaac unspoken (Gen 32)? To this we shall answer that, when the beginning and the end are set down, the middle too is named. …
63:18: Second, he sets out their misery as to slavery: they have possessed your holy people as nothing, that is, without resistance, above: O Lord our God, other lords besides you have had dominion over us (Isa 26:13); as to the profanation of their holy places: our enemies have trodden down your sanctuary: the holy places are come into the hands of strangers (1 Macc 2:8).
Our enemies, he says, have trodden down your sanctuary. There is no doubt that he means the Temple, which the victorious Romans trod down.
63:19: As to the loss of their former honor: we are become, without a king, without the temple, as in the beginning, in Egypt, or even before the calling of Abraham: but you, O Lord, are among us, and your name is called upon by us, forsake us not (Jer 14:9).

And we have become as in the beginning, before we were called in Abraham, and while we were in Egypt, having no God, nor kings, nor princes, nor Prophets, nor the Law of the commandments of God (Hos 3); all of which was fulfilled after the passion of the Lord, and is being fulfilled today. For since they said, His blood be upon us and upon our children (Matt 27:25), an everlasting curse remains, and God does not rule over them, nor is his name called upon them, since they are by no means called the people of God.
63:2:
1101. Why then is your apparel red? Here he sets out the second question, concerning his clothing.

And first, he sets out the question: why then, as if to say: it is not the just, but the wicked who usually bear the marks of blood like this, not saviors, but rather murderers; like theirs that tread in the winepress: for there is red wine in that region that dyes clothing like blood: and Jesus was clothed with filthy garments (Zech 3:3).

Second, he sets out the answer: I have trodden.

 …

Why then is your clothing red, and your garments like those of men treading the winepress? LXX: Why are your garments red, and your clothing like that of men treading the winepress, full and trodden down? Where it now says red, the Hebrew reads EDOM (אדום). So above too, where Edom is written, it is not the name of a place but a word for blood. And again the angels ask and say: We have learned that you are he who speaks righteousness, and that the salvation of all has been placed in your judgment. …
63:4:
1103. For the day of vengeance. Here he goes through the entire order of the matter.

And first, he sets out the suitableness of the time: vengeance, as to the demons; redemption, as to the just, whose recompense had been delayed until then, above: it is the day of the vengeance of the Lord (Isa 34:8).

For the day of vengeance, he says, is in my heart; the year of my redemption has come. Of this we read above too (cf. Isa 61), in a good sense, to preach the acceptable year of the Lord and the day of retribution to our God; and now it is taken both in a bad and in a good sense. In a bad sense: For the day of vengeance is in my heart. …
63:5:
Second, he sets out the necessity of salvation: I looked about, and there was none to help, the human race, who could save it, above: he saw that there is not a man (Isa 59:16); or there was none to help, me on the cross: my brethren have withdrawn from me, and my acquaintance have departed from me (Job 19:13); I looked on my right hand, and beheld, and there was no one that would know me (Ps 141:5[142:4]); they compassed me on every side (Sir 51:10[7]).

 …

He had also said in the psalm: And I looked for one who would grieve with me, and there was none, and for one who would comfort me, and I found none (Ps 68 [69]:21). For he, though he was in the form of God, did not count it robbery to be equal with God, but emptied himself (Phil 2), taking the form of a servant, and became obedient to the Father unto death, even the death of the cross; and therefore he gave him a name above every name, so that he might save for himself by his right hand those who believe in him, …
63:6: Fourth, the exposition of his vengeance: and I have trodden down the people, the Jews, through the Romans, and have made them drunk, filled them with affliction, and have brought down their strength, the Jews and the demons, above: the Lord of hosts has designed it, to pull down the pride of all glory, and bring to disgrace all the glorious ones of the earth (Isa 23:9).
63:7:
1105. I will remember the tender mercies of the Lord. Here the prophet offers a petition to the judge, who comes to speak and fulfill justice.

And first, he inclines him to compassion;

second, he offers his petition, O that you wouldst rend the heavens (ch. 64).

The first of these is divided into two parts:

in the first, he inclines him to compassion by recalling his former benefits, which have passed away;

in the second, by recalling the dangers which they met: why have you made us to err? (Isa 63:17).

 …

I will remember the mercies of the Lord, the praise of the Lord for all that the Lord has rendered to us, and for the multitude of good things to the house of Israel, which he has bestowed on them according to his indulgence and according to the multitude of his mercies. …
63:8: 1106. And first, he recalls the benefits, as to their escape from dangers, recalling his particular election: and he, namely, God, said: surely, although they may be against me, they are children that will not deny, namely, Abraham, or that will not deny, because they at least keep my faith: the Lord is my strength and my praise (Exod 15:2).

And he said: Surely they are my people, sons who do not deny; and he became their Savior. In all their tribulation he was not troubled, and the Angel of his face saved them; in his love and in his indulgence he himself redeemed them, and he bore them and lifted them up all the days of the age. But they provoked him to anger and afflicted the spirit of his Holy One and he was turned to be their enemy, and he himself fought them down. LXX: And he said: Is it not my people? Sons will by no means reject. …
63:9:
And as to his diligent protection: in all their affliction; and he himself was troubled, from compassion; or he was not troubled, right away, but he delayed even now, that they might be corrected; and the angel of his face, that is, the angel that sees my face, saved them, as their leader in the desert: lead this people whither I have told you: my angel shall go before you (Exod 32:34); he has given his angels charge over you; to keep you in all your ways (Ps 90[91]:11).

 …
64:1:
1113. Here he offers a petition. And first, he asks for the presence of the judge; second, he asks for mercy: "behold you are angry" (Isa 64:5). Concerning the first, he does two things. First, he sets out the petition; second, the fulfillment of the petition: "you didst come down" (Isa 64:3). Concerning the first of these, he does two things.

 …

O that you would rend the heavens and come down! At your presence the mountains would flow down. When you do wonders, we shall not endure them; you came down, and at your presence the mountains flowed down. …
