64:12: And he wonders at his patience: "will you refrain yourself, O Lord, upon these things?" "Why look you upon our iniquities?" (Hab 1:13).
64:2:
In the waters: "the waters would burn with fire," because you are all fiery, if you should wish: "at another time the fire, above its own power, burnt in the midst of water" (Wis 16:19); or, by the waters are signified peoples: "the many waters are many peoples" (Rev 17:15).

 …
64:3:
The effect on the Jews: "when you shall do wonderful things, we shall not bear," that is, we, who are accustomed to see and hear, because of our stupor, as they were terrified in Exodus 20:18, thus: "they that had excused themselves" (Heb 12:19); or we shall not bear his coming, even having seen his miracles.

1115. Here he sets out the fulfillment of the petition. And first, as to his coming: "you didst come down," to judge us: using the past tense for the future; or, into the womb of the virgin. …
64:5:
As to the promptness of his benefitting them: "you have met him that rejoices," to help him, while he was still petitioning or coming to you; "him that rejoices," in you: "wisdom goes about seeking such as are worthy of her" (Wis 6:17). Mystically: Simeon (Luke 2).

1117. "Behold you are angry." Here he sets out mercy. And first, he shows the need of the petitioner; second, he offers the petition: "and now, O Lord" (Isa 64:8). Concerning the first, he does two things. …

Behold, you are angry, and we have sinned; in them we have always been, and we shall be saved. And we have become as one unclean all of us, all our righteousnesses as the cloth of a menstruous woman. And we have all fallen like a leaf, and our iniquities, like the wind, have carried us away. …
64:6:
And as to the imperfection of their good deeds: "and we are all become as one unclean, and all our justices," because they are wrapped up in other sins: "if I be washed, as it were, with snow waters, and my hands shall shine ever clean, yet you shall plunge me in filth, and my garments shall abhor me" (Job 9:30-31).

 …
64:7: 1118. He shows the need of the petitioner as to lack of help. And first, lack of human help: "there is none that calls upon" and "takes hold of you," with prayers: "I held him: and I will not let him go" (Song 3:4); second, lack of divine help: "you have hid your face," of your mercy, "and have crushed us in the hand," that is, the work, of our iniquity; according to what it says in Proverbs 18:21: "I will hide my face from them" (Deut 32:20).

There is none who calls upon your name, who rises up and takes hold of you. You have hidden your face from us, and have dashed us down in the hand of our iniquity. LXX: And there is none who calls upon your name, and who, remembering, lays hold of you. For you have turned away your face from us, and have handed us over because of our iniquities. …
64:8: 1119. "And now, O Lord." Here he sets out mercy. And concerning this, he does two things. First, he asks for mercy, assigning the reason: "you are our father": "as clay is in the hand of the potter, so are we in the hand of God" (Jer 18:6); "remember, I beseech you, that you have made me as the clay" (Job 10:9).

And now, O Lord, you are our father, and we are clay; and you are our fashioner, and we are all the works of your hands. Do not be angry, O Lord, exceedingly, and do not remember iniquity any longer. Behold, look: we are all your people. The city of your Holy One has become a desert; Zion has become a desert, Jerusalem desolate. The house of our sanctification and of our glory, where our fathers praised you, has been made a burning of fire, and all our desirable things have been turned into ruin. …
64:9: And now, O Lord. Here he sets out mercy. And concerning this, he does two things. First, he asks for mercy, assigning the reason: you are our father: as clay is in the hand of the potter, so are we in the hand of God (Jer 18:6); remember, I beseech you, that you have made me as the clay (Job 10:9). And he offers the petition: be not angry enough, that is, exceedingly, or according to what our merits demand: remember not our former iniquities: let your mercies speedily prevent us (Ps 78[79]:8). …
65:1: They have sought me. Here the judge, namely, God, gives the sentence of the separation of the wicked from the good, in the reception of the promised salvation. And this is divided into two parts: in the first, he pronounces the sentence of separation; in the second, he determines the manner of execution: thus says the Lord (ch. 66). Concerning the first, he does two things. …

They sought me who before did not ask for me: they found, who did not seek me. I said: Behold me, behold me, to a nation that did not call upon my name. LXX: I appeared to those not seeking me: I was found by those who did not ask for me. I said: Behold me, in a nation that did not call upon my name. To the prayer of the people mingled with complaints, in which it had said: Why have you made us err, O Lord, from your way: you have hardened our hearts, so that we did not fear you (Isa 63:17)? …
65:10: Third, as to the fertility of their pastures: and the plains, and the valley of Achor, so called, because they stoned Achan there (Josh 7:24–26); I will give them the valley of Achor for an opening of hope (Hos 2:15).

And there shall be, he says, plains, or woodlands, as folds for flocks. For plains, SARON (שרון) is put in the Hebrew. The whole region around Lydda, Joppa and Jamnia is suited to pasturing flocks. Of it it is also written in the Acts of the Apostles: But the woodlands shall be turned into sheepfolds (Acts 9), according to what is sung in the psalm: The voice of the Lord perfecting the stags, and he will lay bare the woodlands (Ps 28 [29]:9), or the thickets of the forests, so that robbers may cease to lurk there, …
65:11: And you, that have forsaken. Here he separates the wicked from the consolation of the good, because of their sins of omission. And first, he threatens punishment for the wicked; second, he promises rewards for the good: because the former distresses are forgotten (Isa 65:16). Concerning the first, he does two things. …

And you who have forsaken the Lord, and have forgotten my holy mountain; who set a table for fortune, and pour libations upon it: I will number you for the sword, and you shall all fall in the slaughter. LXX: But you who have forsaken me, and have forgotten my holy mountain, and prepare a table for fortune, and fill a drink for the demon: I will hand you over to the sword: you shall all fall slain. …
65:12: And he sets out the punishment: I will number you in the sword, as if to say: so that none remain who will not be crushed: they shall fall by the sword, and by the famine (Jer 44:12). Second, because they did not obey when they were called back, and he sets out the fault: because I called and you did not answer: I called, and you refused (Prov 1:24).

Because I called, and you did not answer; I spoke, and you did not hear: but you did evil in my eyes, and what I did not will, you chose. LXX: Because I called you, and you did not hear: I spoke, and you despised, and you did evil in my sight, and what I did not will you chose. …
65:13: And he threatens the punishment of separation. First, in satisfaction of the body: therefore thus says the Lord God: behold my servants shall eat, and you shall be hungry: the rich have wanted, and have suffered hunger: but they that seek the Lord shall not be deprived of any good (Ps 33:11[34:10]).

Therefore thus says the Lord God: Behold, my servants shall eat, and you shall be hungry. Behold, my servants shall drink, and you shall be thirsty. Behold, my servants shall rejoice, and you shall be put to shame. Behold, my servants shall give praise for exultation of heart, and you shall cry out for sorrow of heart, and for contrition of spirit you shall howl. LXX: Therefore thus says the Lord: Behold, my servants shall eat, but you shall be hungry. Behold, my servants shall drink, but you shall be thirsty. …
65:14: Second, in joy of heart: behold my servants shall rejoice, and you shall be confounded: repenting, and groaning for anguish of spirit (Wis 5:3).

And the contrition of spirit for sorrow of heart is to be understood of the conscience of sins, according to what is written: Those who err in spirit shall know understanding (Isa 29:24). And: A contrite and humbled heart, O God, you will not despise (Ps 50 [51]:19). The spirit is crushed when it has been lifted up; as is written of a king hostile to Israel: The Lord hardened his spirit (2 Kgs 17:14). …
65:15: Third, in difference of name, and first, he sets out the sort of name the impious shall have: and you shall leave your name for an oath to my elect, that they might confirm their words thus: if it is not so, so shall it happen to me as happened to them: by the sword, and by the famine shall they die: and they shall be for an oath, and for a wonder, and for a curse, and for a reproach (Jer 44:12). …

And you shall leave your name for an oath to my elect, and the Lord God shall slay you, and he shall call his servants by another name, in which he who is blessed upon the earth shall be blessed in God, amen: and he who swears in the earth shall swear in God, amen. LXX: For you shall leave your name for satiety to my elect. …
65:16: Because the former distresses are forgotten. Here he promises rewards seen. And first, in general, as to the removal of evils: because the former distresses are forgotten, not because of lack of knowledge, but because they have been succeeded by good things, above: you shall forget the shame of your youth (Isa 54:4).

For the former distresses have been given over to oblivion, and because they are hidden from my eyes. For behold, I create new heavens and a new earth, and the former things shall not be in memory: and it shall not come up upon the heart: but you shall rejoice and exult forever in the things that I create. LXX: For they shall forget the former tribulation, and it shall not come up upon their heart. …
65:17: And as to the restoration of goods: for behold I create new heavens, new help from heaven, and a new earth, new benefits from the earth; or this refers to the day of judgment, when the world will be renewed to the glory of the saints: the former things are passed away (Rev 21:4).

The eighteenth book on Isaiah, or rather the last, is dedicated to your name, O daughter Eustochium, and to that of your holy mother Paula, so that I may now recall with equal remembrance those whom I have looked up to with equal honor: especially since she too, while she lived, often asked for this work together with you, and your brother Pammachius, a most learned man, did not cease, both then and afterwards, to press me with frequent letters; and for me there is one and the same devotion toward friends present …
65:18: Second, in particular: for behold I create Jerusalem. And first, as to cheerfulness of heart: Jerusalem, earthly Jerusalem, but more, the heavenly Jerusalem; <a rejoicing, that is,> rejoicing, emphatically, so that all things are absorbed in joy, above: they shall obtain joy and gladness, and sorrow and mourning shall flee away (Isa 35:10).

For behold, I create Jerusalem an exultation, and its people a joy: and I will exult in Jerusalem, and rejoice in my people. LXX: For behold, I make Jerusalem an exultation, and my people a gladness, and I will exult over Jerusalem, and be glad over my people. …
65:2: Second, he sentences separation: I have spread forth my hands. And first, he sentences the separation of the wicked from the good, because of sins of transgression; second, because of sins of omission: and you, that have forsaken (Isa 65:11). The first of these is divided into two: in the first, he threatens punishment for the wicked; in the second, he promises rewards for the good: thus says the Lord (Isa 65:8). …

I have spread out my hands all the day to an unbelieving people, who walk in a way not good, after their own thoughts. LXX: I have spread out my hands all the day to an unbelieving and contradicting people, who have not walked in the good way, but after their sins. …
65:21: Third, as to prosperity of goods, both as to security of their possessions: and they shall build: and they shall build houses (Ezek 28:26); they shall plant vineyards (Amos 9:14).

And they shall build houses, and dwell in them; and they shall plant vineyards, and eat their fruits. They shall not build, and another dwell: they shall not plant, and another eat. LXX likewise. Of these houses the prophetic word also makes promise in Psalm 68 (69), saying: For God will save Zion: and the cities of Judah shall be built, and they shall dwell there, and acquire it by inheritance, and the seed of his servants shall possess it: and those who love his name shall dwell in it. …
65:23: And as to the peace of their children: nor bring forth in trouble, as though bringing forth children into servitude to their enemies: good things continue with their seed (Sir 44:11).

These shall not labor in vain, as the Jews once labored; but they shall eat the labors of their hands. Nor shall they bring forth in trouble, or for a curse, or, as is put more expressly in the Hebrew, εἰς ἀνυπαρξίαν, which in their language is said LABALA (לבהלה), that is, so that they cease to be and have an end of their substance: for which Aquila, Symmachus and Theodotion translated haste: so that they may by no means hasten to believe without reason, but may imitate Nathanael, who was praised by the voice of …
65:24: Fourth, as to the hearing of their prayers: and it shall come to pass, that before they call, with their mouth, above: at the voice of your cry, as soon as he shall hear, he will answer you (Isa 30:19).

When these cry out, they will at once be heard, and while they are speaking the Lord will say, Here I am. All of which we see fulfilled even according to the letter in the Acts of the Apostles. For all the nations could not have believed in so short a time unless their faith had in some way been wrung from them by the miracles of signs. …
65:25: Fifth, as to the tranquility of peace: the wolf and the lamb, for those who formerly were tyrants and evildoers will abide peacefully with others, above (Isa 11:6) has the same.

Then the wolf and the lamb fed together, Paul the persecutor and Ananias the disciple (Acts 9). He is the wolf of whom it is written: Benjamin, a ravening wolf, in the morning shall eat the prey, and at evening shall give food (Gen 49:27); or, as it is said in the Hebrew, shall divide the spoils. His teaching was the food of believers, and he triumphed over his vanquished adversaries in the whole world. …
65:3: Second, from the continuity of their sinning: a people that continually provoke me to anger before my face, for all things are naked and open to his eyes (Heb 4:13), or because they placed idols in the temple: they have provoked me with that which was no god (Deut 32:21). Third, from the variety or seriousness of their sins, as to four things. …

A people that provokes me to anger, before my face always: who sacrifice in gardens, and offer sacrifice upon bricks (From Exod 20:4). LXX: This people that embitters me in my sight: they always sacrifice in gardens, and burn incense upon brick ÷ to demons that are not. ⁚ Though the Lord says: You shall not make for yourself an idol, nor a likeness of anything that is in heaven, and that is upon the earth. …
65:4: Second, as to their enthusiasm for divinations: that dwell in sepulchers, that they might have answers from the dead; in the temples (delubris), temples of idols so called from diluendo ("washing"), for they thought all things were washed away there; or because of the fonts, which were there for washing the victims and priests; and sleep, upon the hides of the victims for the purpose of divination: your temples shall be destroyed (Ezek 6:6). …

Who dwell in tombs, and sleep in the shrines of idols: who eat swine's flesh, and profane broth is in their vessels: who say, Depart from me, do not come near me, for you are unclean. LXX: In tombs and in caves they sleep for the sake of dreams: who eat swine's flesh and the broth of victims; all their vessels are profane: who say, Go far from me, do not come near me, for I am clean. …
65:6: Second, the certainty of punishment: behold it is written, for their sin is firmly in memory, and their punishment in preordination; I will not be silent, overlooking their sins: the sin of Judah is written (Jer 17:1), above: I have held my peace, always I have kept silence (Isa 42:14).

Behold, he says, it is written before me. For all our sins lie open to the eyes of God, and are written in those books of which we read in Daniel: Thrones were set, and the books were opened (Dan 7:10). Of which it is said in another place: Let them be written upon the earth (Jer 17:13). And he will by no means keep silent any longer, he who had said before: I have kept silent: shall I always keep silent? says the Lord (Isa 42:14). …
65:7: Third, the multitude of the punishments, because they are for all the sins of their fathers: but I will render: I am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children (Exod 20:5). Who have reproached me, by adoring idols in the high places; and also for the sins of their youth: and I will measure back their first work, as if to say, I will make the punishment commensurate to the fault, above: she has received of the hand of the Lord double (Isa 40:2).

For we ought not to take as fathers, whose iniquities and sins are now repaid to us, those from whose seed our bodies were born. Otherwise Moses himself, who had said that the sins of the fathers are to be repaid to the sons to the third and fourth generation of those who hate God (Exod 20), interprets his own sentence, saying: The sons shall not die for the sins of the fathers: but each shall die in his own sin (Deut 24:16). …
65:8: Thus says the Lord. Here he promises rewards to the good. And first, as to their preservation from evils: as if a grain, of a grape; it is a blessing, that is, it pleases God for it to be reserved for a blessing; for the sake of my servants, your fathers; that I may not destroy the whole, people of the Jews, above: it shall be as when one gathers (Isa 17:5) clusters in the vintage.

Thus says the Lord: As if a grain is found in a cluster, and it is said: Do not destroy it, for it is a blessing; so will I do for the sake of my servants, that I may not destroy the whole. LXX: Thus says the Lord: As if a grape is found in a cluster, and it is said: Do not touch it, for there is a blessing in it: so will I do for the sake of my servant, that I may not destroy all. …
65:9: Second, as to their advancement in good things. And first, as to the multiplication of their seed: and I will bring forth a seed out of Jacob, above: except the Lord of hosts had left us seed, we had been as Sodom (Isa 1:9). Second, as to the restoration of the inheritance of their fathers: and my elect shall inherit it: they shall possess you for their inheritance: and you shall be their inheritance (Ezek 36:12).

And I will bring forth a seed out of Jacob, and out of Judah one possessing my mountains: and my elect shall inherit it, and my servants shall dwell there, and the plains shall be folds for flocks, and the valley of Achor a resting place for herds, for my people who have sought me. …
66:10: Second, he promises immense comfort to the gathered Jews. And first, he invites others to congratulation: rejoice with Jerusalem, and be glad with her, as in the object of joy, setting out the condition of congratulation as to affection: all you that love her: eat, O friends, and drink, and be inebriated, my dearly beloved (Song 5:1); as to the sign of affection: all you that mourn for her: blessed are they that mourn: for they shall be comforted (Matt 5:5).

Rejoice with Jerusalem, and exult in her, all you who love her. Rejoice with her with joy, all you who mourn over her, that you may suck and be filled from the breast of her consolation, that you may milk and abound with delights from her glory of every kind. LXX: Rejoice, Jerusalem, and make an assembly, all you who love her. …
66:11: And the fruit of congratulation as to participation in her gladness or peace: that you may suck: your breasts are better than wine (Song 1:1); as to participation in her glory, that you may milk out, as though extracting milk: then shall you abound in delights in the Almighty (Job 22:6).

For it could not be that she who had borne a male and had just given birth should lack an abundance of milk for the rearing of that nation and of the little ones who had been born at once, so that she might offer them two breasts, by no means, as formerly in Egypt, broken and lying low, but whole and standing in virginal beauty, those of the Old and New Instrument, to supply rational milk. Of these the bridegroom speaks to her: Your breasts are better than wine (Song 1:1). …
66:12:
Second, he promises an abundant gathering of peace: for thus says the Lord: behold I will bring upon her, so that an overflowing is called, as a river descending with great force comes and does not overflow; and of glory: and as an overflowing torrent, above: your peace had been as a river (Isa 48:18).

Third, he promises full reception of comfort. …

For thus says the Lord: Behold, I turn upon her as it were a river of peace, and as an overflowing torrent the glory of the nations, which you shall suck: you shall be carried at the breast, and upon the knees they shall caress you. LXX: For thus says the Lord: Behold, I will turn toward them like a river of peace, and like a torrent overflowing the glory of the nations. Their little ones shall be carried on the shoulders, and upon the knees they shall be comforted. …
66:13: Second, as to divine protection: as one whom the mother caresses: you have forgotten the consolation (Heb 12:5).

As one whom a mother caresses, so will I comfort you, and in Jerusalem you shall be comforted. You shall see, and your heart shall rejoice, and your bones shall sprout like grass. And the hand of the Lord shall be known to his servants, and he shall be indignant with his enemies. For servants the LXX put those who fear; for enemies, the unbelieving: the rest likewise. …
66:14:
Third, as to the enjoyment of goods, you shall see good things given to you by God; bones, you who in adversity were like dry bones: you dry bones, hear the word of the Lord (Ezek 37:4). Or you shall see the divine essence: the light is sweet, and it is delightful for the eyes to see the sun (Eccl 11:7); and your bones shall flourish like an herb, in the resurrection.

And the hand of the Lord shall be known. Here he promises punishment to the wicked. …

After these have been comforted, it will be said to them: And you shall see, and your heart shall rejoice, and your bones shall sprout like grass, or shall spring up, or according to Symmachus, shall flourish (John 16:22). And they shall see, without doubt, God, which is true gladness. Of these the Lord spoke: Blessed are the pure in heart, for they shall see God (Matt 5:8). …
66:15: And he sets out the magnitude of the punishment: for behold the Lord will come with fire, by which the city is to be burned, or by which the world is to be purified; and his chariots, the army of the Chaldeans, in which God comes, as it were, or the angels, who will come with him for judgment: a fire shall go before him (Ps 96[97]:3).

For behold, the Lord will come in fire: and his chariots like a whirlwind, to render his fury in indignation, and his rebuke in a flame of fire. For in fire the Lord is judged, and with his sword unto all flesh: and those slain by the Lord shall be multiplied. LXX: Behold, the Lord will come as fire, and his chariots as a tempest, to render his vengeance in fury: and his rebuke in a flame of fire. …
66:16: They shall fall by the sword of God (Amos 9:10). And he sets out the multitude of those who are punished: the slain of the Lord shall be many, above: for there is a victim of the Lord in Bosra and a great slaughter in the land of Edom (Isa 34:6).

And so in this fire and fury, in these chariots and in the flame of fire all flesh shall be judged, or the Lord himself with his creatures, so that he may be seen to pass sentence not by power but by the truth of judgment, according to what is said at greater length in Micah and more briefly in Psalm 50 (51): That you may be justified in your words, and may prevail when you are judged (Ps 50 [51]:5). …
66:17: Second, he reproaches their fault: they that were sanctified, thinking to cleanse themselves of uncleanness by the waters, or even by the sacrifices of idols, in the gardens, in which they worshipped idols, or occupied themselves with pleasure; behind one woman, copulating with women in the manner of beasts, or behind the gate, in other manuscripts; the mouse, the dormouse, contrary to the law (Lev 11:29), above: that eat swine's flesh, and profane broth (Isa 65:4).

Those who were sanctified, and thought themselves clean in the gardens behind one within: who ate swine's flesh, and the abomination, and the mouse, shall be consumed together, says the Lord. LXX: Those who are sanctified and purified in the gardens and on the thresholds: eating pig's flesh, and abominations, and the mouse: they shall be consumed together, says the Lord. …
66:18: But I. Here he describes the manner of separation as to everyone together. And first, he decrees universal judgment: I know their works, and their thoughts, as though judging them for both; I come, in the day of judgment, or the various kingdoms of your enemies destroying also the wicked among you; they shall come, into Jerusalem after your return, either to judgment, or to faith: behold, I will raise them up out of the place wherein you have sold them (Joel 3:7).

The Lord comes, then, to gather the works and thoughts of each. From this we learn that not only works but thoughts too are to be judged on the day of judgment. For he who has looked on a woman to lust after her has already committed adultery with her in his heart (Matt 5). …
66:19: Second, he sets out the summons to judgment: and I will set a sign, the edict of Cyrus, among them, that is, the Jews who were with Zorobabel and the other leaders; to the Gentiles, to the nations whom the Jews had been dispersed; Lydia them that draw the bow, for they are good archers; my glory, which will appear in your liberation, above: he shall set up a sign unto the nations (Isa 11:12). …

But I come to gather their works and their thoughts together with all the nations and tongues: and they shall come and see my glory. And I will set a sign among them, and I will send of those who have been saved to the nations in the sea, to Africa, to Lydia, those who draw the arrow, to Italy and Greece, to the islands far off: to those who have not heard of me, and have not seen my glory. …
66:20: Third, he sets out the preparation of those to be judged. And first, as to the good; second, as to the wicked: and they shall go out, and see (Isa 66:22). The first of these is divided into two parts. First, as to the Jews, he sets out their honorable return: and they shall bring all your brethren out upon horses, by which are signified the reinforcements they reverently received from the gentiles: the Lord will bring them to you (Bar 5:6); or by which are signified the various conditions of those who are …

And they shall announce my glory among the nations, and they shall bring all your brothers from all the nations as a gift to the Lord, on horses, and in four-horse chariots, and in litters, and on mules, and in carriages, to my holy mountain Jerusalem, says the Lord. LXX: And they shall announce my glory among the nations: and they shall bring your brothers from all the nations as a gift to the Lord, with horses and wagons, in the lampenae of mules, with canopies, into the holy city Jerusalem, says the Lord. …
66:21: Second, the exaltation of their return, first, as to their worthiness: and I will take of them to be priests, which was literally fulfilled in the Jews, and also in the apostles, above: you shall be called the priests of the Lord: to you it shall be said: you ministers of our God (Isa 61:6).

And I will take, he says, of them priests and Levites, says the Lord: so that those who have been saved may preach to the nations. One of these said: So let a man reckon us as ministers of Christ, and stewards of the mysteries of God (1 Cor 4:1). And Luke the evangelist: As they delivered to us, he says, who from the beginning saw and were ministers of the word. Of these we also read above: You shall be to me priests of the Lord (Isa 61:6). …
66:22: Second, as to the preservation of their seed: for as the new heavens, as above, so shall your seed stand (Isa 65:17), forever: if these ordinances shall fail before me, says the Lord: then also the seed of Israel shall fail (Jer 31:36); or the saints will stand eternally renewed as heaven and earth.

For as the new heavens and the new earth, which I make to stand before me, says the Lord: so shall your seed stand, and your name. And it shall be month from month, and sabbath from sabbath: all flesh shall come to worship before my face, says the Lord. LXX: For as the new heaven and the new earth, which I make to remain in my sight, says the Lord: so shall your seed stand and your name. And it shall be month from month, and sabbath from sabbath: all flesh shall come to worship the Lord in my sight in Jerusalem. …
66:23:
Third, as to the duration of their glory: and there shall be month after month, as if to say, month will follow month and feast will follow feast in your prosperity, above: year is added to year: the solemnities are at an end (Isa 29:1). Mystically: the Church after the end, spiritual rest after carnal rest.

 …

And it shall be, he says, month from month, and sabbath from sabbath: so that out of carnal sabbaths and months there may come spiritual and delightful sabbaths, which sabbath-rest is reserved for the people of God. And a spiritual month, when the moon is filled from point to point and runs its course, so as to make a month, that is, the kalends, which in Greek are called νεομηνίαι, that is, the beginning of a new month; among whom the beginning of the kalends begins and ends not according to the course of the sun …
66:3: Second, he excludes the confidence that they took from their rites of sacrifice. And first, he sets out their rejection: he that sacrifices an ox, is as if he slew a man, as if to say: their sacrifices are so abominable, as if they were doing something against the law, because they were offering them to idols; as if he should bless, praise and venerate, an idol, above: offer sacrifice no more in vain (Isa 1:13). …

And what follows in the common edition: But the wicked man, is not found in the Hebrew, but it simply joins on and says: He who sacrifices an ox is as one who kills a man. This is also written in another place: I desire mercy, and not sacrifice: the knowledge of God rather than holocaust (Hos 6:6). And through Malachi: All that I hated, you did: covering my altar with tears: is it fitting that I should look upon your sacrifice, and receive anything acceptable from your hands (Mal 2:13)? …
66:4: Second, he threatens punishment: wherefore I also will choose their mockeries: he shall scorn the scorners (Prov 3:34); the fear which I feared, has come upon me: and that which I was afraid of, has befallen me (Job 3:25).
